text:
maria_customer: Hi team — our realtime streaming endpoint keeps dropping after ~55s. Last SSE chunk is partial and client reports EOF. We're behind Cloudflare then an ALB -> NLB origin in eu-west-1. This is impacting production users and spiking billing because clients reconnect repeatedly. Request id r-9a7c3f.

ana_support: Sorry you're seeing this. Can you paste a minimal repro curl and the exact headers you send? Also confirm Cloudflare + ALB in front — any WAF or bot rules?

maria_customer: Repro below (sanitized keys):

curl -v -N \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  'https://api.redwood-cust.example/v1/realtime?model=rwd-small-1.0'

Observed behavior: streaming begins, tokens stream for ~50–56s, final chunk arrives partial (truncated JSON), then TCP connection closed by peer. Client log: "recv(): Connection reset by peer". No "data: [DONE]".

ana_support: Thanks. Do you see any 502/504 from Cloudflare or ALB logs? Also what Content-Encoding and Transfer headers are present?

maria_customer: No 502/504 reported to our client — just abrupt close. We saw a single Cloudflare 522 in a different account around that time, but nothing consistent. Headers we send: Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Connection: keep-alive, Accept: text/event-stream. We do not set any explicit SSE heartbeat.

jay_oncall: Ping — can you paste the exact elapsed time when connection closes? ALB default idle_timeout is 60s — if the origin is silent >60s ALB will close. Cloudflare has its own timeouts (100s). But if there's a chain (CF -> ALB -> NLB -> origin) half-close behavior can drop mid-chunk.

maria_customer: It consistently dies at 54–57s after start. We have intermittent longer streams but the vast majority end in that window.

ben_infra: Can you confirm whether TLS is terminated at Cloudflare or ALB? If Cloudflare does TLS and talks HTTP to ALB, ALB might see a keepalive gap and close. Also check if the ALB idle timeout was modified — default 60s but some infra sets 30s.

li_network: We pulled our edge traces for r-9a7c3f — connection flow CF -> ALB -> NLB -> origin. ALB logs show a Target:Idled event with target_response_time ~56.1s and then a connection close. That matches an idle timeout. ALB closed the connection mid-transfer (half-close) which likely caused the partial chunk on the client.

ana_support: Ok that points to an ALB idle timeout. Short-term workaround: add an SSE heartbeat from the origin every 15s (send a comment event or zero-length chunk) so ALB/CF see activity. Also set headers to disable buffering: e.g. for nginx: "X-Accel-Buffering: no" and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is preserved.

maria_customer: Are there any Redwood-side headers we should add? We can't change ALB config.

jay_oncall: We can inject a lightweight heartbeat header from our runtime: add periodic ":", or "data: \"\n\"\n" comments every 10s. But easier: ask infra to bump ALB idle_timeout to 180s or enable TCP keepalive between ALB and target. If Cloudflare is in front, also enable CF Origin Keepalive to avoid idle windows.

ben_infra: Actionable items: 1) We can temporarily bump ALB idle_timeout for this customer to 180s (Ben). 2) Add origin SSE heartbeat in runtime as config flag (Jay). 3) Ask customer to disable buffering headers at their frontend if they have an additional proxy.

li_network: Note on billing: repeated reconnects cause duplicate request counts; we saw a customer session pattern where reconnects doubled token billing for same user. Sam, any billing policy for duplicate reconnections during outages?

sam_billing: We can investigate credits if ruling shows client reconnects due to our edge closing. Please send the invoice id and the request ids/time windows. If it's our misconfig (ALB default we control), we'll issue a credit.

maria_customer: Quick test we ran: same curl but with an explicit client-side keepalive (sends ping every 20s) — the stream stayed alive for 6 minutes. Seems to confirm idle close.

ana_support: Good repro. For completeness, please capture tcpdump of the final seconds (if possible) so we can see RST vs FIN. If it's FIN from ALB it's graceful close after idle. If RST it's abrupt.

maria_customer: I'll capture and upload logs. One more detail: when the client reconnects, the second connection sometimes returns 401 for the same token. That was a separate auth race — token rotation on our side; we rotate short-lived tokens on reconnect. Might be contributing.

jay_oncall: That's important — reconnect+auth rotation can cause partial transcripts lost. Two parallel fixes: heartbeat + extend ALB idle; and ensure clients retry with same token or handle 401 by refreshing and resuming. We'll add a note in docs about token expiry and streaming reconnect semantics.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: origin/runtime:stream-heartbeat v2.3.1 -> eu-west-1 at 1745234800

ben_infra: I've temporarily set ALB idle_timeout=180s for the affected target group and disabled proxy buffering on the nginx ingress. Please try again and report.

maria_customer: Re-tested at 17:28 UTC — streams now persist >4 minutes, final chunk intact, no partial JSON. Billing spike stopped. Huge thanks.

ana_support: Marking this resolved pending your confirmation after 24h. Owners: ben_infra (ALB change), jay_oncall (heartbeat config), sam_billing (billing review), maria_customer (verify).

sam_billing: I'll open a billing review ticket and flag for potential credit; need request ids + time window when reconnect flood happened.

ana_support: Closing note: root cause = ALB idle timeout + no origin SSE heartbeat + chain with Cloudflare causing mid-chunk half-close. Workarounds: heartbeat every 10–15s, ALB idle_timeout bump, disable proxy buffering.
